kimi_k3/001:
This policy is a **tactically-aware heuristic Go engine with a 2–3 ply search**:

1. **Board model**: 21×21 padded 1‑D board for cheap neighbor lookups, with incremental-stamp flood fills to compute groups and liberties fast.
2. **Legality**: full suicide detection, plus **positional superko** via a global history of bitboard hashes (reset automatically between games), so we can never return an illegal ko recapture.
3. **Candidate generation**: all empty points within Chebyshev distance 2 of any stone, plus corner/star points in the opening.
4. **Move features**: captures, saving own atari groups, putting enemy groups in atari, self-atari/low-liberty penalties, connection & cut bonuses, reinforcement of 2-liberty groups, and an opening prior (3rd/4th line, star points, approach distances, invasion caution).
5. **Search**: the top ~14–24 moves by heuristic score get a deeper look — full-board area evaluation (stones + regions touching one color), the opponent's best tactical reply (captures/ataris via "tactical points" = liberties of groups with ≤2 liberties), and our best counter-reply (catching snapbacks and recaptures). The move maximizing `my_score + eval_gain − 0.9·opponent_reply` is chosen.
6. **Passing**: only passes when ahead and every remaining move is a worthless own-territory fill late in the game; otherwise always returns a legal move, with a safe fallback path.

A time guard (0.85 s) adaptively widens/narrows the search so we never time out.
kimi_k3/002: Strategy: a fast one‑ply heuristic search. Rebuild the board, compute connected groups/liberties once, and derive for every empty point tactical features (capture size of adjacent enemy groups in atari, saving own atari groups, putting 2‑liberty enemy groups into atari, connecting/cutting, estimated liberties after the move). Generate the legal move set; if it is large, rank it with a cheap score (tactics + corner/star‑point opening prior + proximity to the fight) and keep the top candidates (always keeping every capture/atari‑save). Each kept move is then simulated (with captures removed and undone) and scored by a full static evaluation: area estimate using multi‑source BFS influence distances to decide empty‑point ownership, plus group‑safety terms that heavily punish leaving our own groups in atari while only mildly crediting enemy ataris (since the opponent moves next). A small opening prior (4‑4/3‑4 corner points, side stars; penalize 1st/2nd line) is decayed as the game progresses. The best legal move is returned; any exception falls back to a guaranteed‑legal liberty‑holding point, else pass.
kimi_k3/003: The policy is a fast tactical/positional Go player. It generates moves near the action, adds urgent liberties of groups in atari or near-atari, simulates each candidate with suicide and simple-ko prevention, then scores the result with a board evaluation: capture bonuses, group-liberty health, snapback/self-atari risk, distance-transform influence, opening corner/side tables, connection bonuses, and penalties for filling true eyes. It passes only when no candidate is worthwhile.
kimi_k3/004: The strategy is a fast tactical one-ply Go policy: build exact group/liberty information, simulate every legal empty point, reject suicides and likely simple-ko recaptures, then score moves by captures, saving own atari groups, creating atari/cuts, safe connections, liberty quality, eye-filling penalties, and a corner/side fuseki table. It passes only late when every move looks harmful.
kimi_k3/005: The strategy is a fast one-ply tactical evaluator: rebuild groups/liberties, order candidates by urgency, simulate each candidate exactly for captures and suicide, then score captures, saving low-liberty groups, creating atari, connection/cutting, liberties/shape, opening corner-side value, and penalties for filling solid territory or risky snapbacks. It also avoids direct one-stone ko recaptures and has a time-guarded legal fallback.
